headline: The FDA has cleared Neurora, an AI tool that helps doctors diagnose autism in children aged 18 months to 12 years from a recorded assessment.
score_reason: Regulatory clearance of a clinical AI aid, but no accuracy data reported and it supports rather than replaces diagnosis; kept at the curator score.
importance_line: Gives clinicians an objective measure to support autism assessments for children and families, but it is an aid to judgment, and the article gives no figures on how accurate it is.
summary: Medical Device Network reports that the US Food and Drug Administration has cleared Argus Cognitive's Neurora, software that analyses more than 100 vocal, facial and gaze measures from a recorded behavioural assessment to show how closely a child's behaviour matches that of children with and without an autism diagnosis. It is meant to be read alongside the clinician's other findings, not as a standalone diagnosis, and the company's clinical lead says "the clinician still makes the call".
notes: Company release on Business Wire dated 8 Oct 2026 (not fetched). Quote spelled per article: Latha Valluripalli.
